page: Amazon Web Services c8id.large is an entry-level compute-optimized instance hosted on the AWS Nitro system. It is powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor running at a base clock speed of 3.9 GHz on x86_64 architecture. The virtual machine configuration provisions two vCPUs across a single physical core with hyperthreading enabled, paired with 4.0 GB of DDR5 system memory operating at 7 GHz. In addition to 480 MB of shared L3 cache, the hardware architecture includes modern instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX). Local storage is directly bundled as a 118 GB NVMe SSD instance store volume, alongside a baseline network throughput of 1 Gbps.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong single-threaded execution performance, placing its Geekbench single-core rating in the top 25% alongside high throughput in compression tasks such as single-threaded gzip and bzip3 decompression. However, aggregate parallel processing is constrained by the two-vCPU count, resulting in lower-tier placement in multi-core metrics, PassMark scores, and large-block memory bandwidth tests. Static web serving and Redis key-value workloads similarly register lower comparative figures due to overall memory and interface limits, though small language model token generation achieves steady mid-range throughput via updated vector extensions.

Balancing entry-tier resource footprint against modern x86 CPU capabilities, c8id.large delivers cost-efficient computing for tasks that require high single-thread clock rates and fast scratch space. Because it lacks a dedicated GPU and provides 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU, memory-dense enterprise services or heavy parallel data pipelines are unsuitable. The instance is primarily suited for lightweight continuous integration workers, single-threaded processing scripts, lightweight web serving, and localized caching or temporary database staging reliant on integrated NVMe storage.
description: Amazon Web Services c8id.large is a compute-optimized instance built on the Nitro platform, featuring a 3.9 GHz Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor configured with 2 vCPUs across a single physical core. The instance provides 4.0 GB of DDR5 memory alongside 118 GB of integrated NVMe SSD local storage and 1 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Supporting AVX-512 and AMX instruction sets, it delivers upper-quartile performance in single-threaded compute tasks, including compression and Geekbench single-core execution. Overall parallel throughput and memory bandwidth remain modest given the dual-vCPU ceiling and 2.0 GB memory-per-core ratio. Without an attached GPU, c8id.large represents a cost-efficient platform for workloads prioritizing clock speed and fast local ephemeral storage over heavy parallelism, such as continuous integration tasks, localized batch processing, and lightweight microservices.
